Parvaz helps you open websites that your network blocks. You use it with Chrome or another Chromium-based browser, such as Brave, Edge or Vivaldi. Parvaz sends your browser\'s traffic to a relay. A relay is a small program on a Google account, set up by you or by a technical helper you trust. The relay fetches the websites for you. Most other apps, such as banking, messaging and streaming apps, do not accept the certificate you install during setup, so they do not work through Parvaz.

Whoever runs your relay, and Google, can read what passes through it. This includes the addresses you visit, your cookies, and what you type into forms, passwords included. Use Parvaz only with a relay you trust completely.
Cocode runs no server for Parvaz and receives nothing from the app. Parvaz has no account, no analytics, no ads and no crash reporting. Your access key is stored on your phone in encrypted storage.
See the source code on GitHub

Parvaz is free software. You can use, read, change and share it under the MIT license.
Parvaz\'s client is a rewrite of MasterHttpRelayVPN, by Amin Mahmoudi.
The tunnel uses tun2socks, an open-source library that moves your phone\'s traffic into the app.
The app is built with AndroidX and Jetpack Compose (Apache-2.0).
